subject: Marketplace private offer — usage anchor and reseller uplift clarification
messages:
From: James Porter <james.porter@helixhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — usage flex anchor & channel uplift details

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're interested in moving forward with a private offer for Azure Marketplace but need clarity on two items before procurement can sign:

1) Usage anchor / minimums: our platform usage is spiky month-to-month. Can you confirm how a usage floor would be instrumented on the PO (node-hour vs token-month anchor)? We want a short first-year runway rather than a high committed floor.

2) Channel uplift / reseller margin: our reseller (Cloudwise) needs a clear passback path and an explicit uplift percentage on invoice. Can you share the invoice routing and whether the uplift is a gross line item or netted against list price?

Attached is our initial SOW draft (Helix_SOW_v1.pdf) for context. Would appreciate a quick written response we can pass to procurement.

Thanks,
James
James Porter
Head of Procurement, Helix Health
procurement@helixhealth.com

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — usage flex anchor & channel uplift details

James —

Appreciate the SOW. Quick answers up front:

- Anchor: we can anchor on node-hour commitments or usage units (token-month). For spiky workloads most customers prefer a small node-hour anchor with a large metered band — we can structure a 3-month ramp that smooths over spikes.

- Channel uplift: we support both explicit uplift line items on the reseller invoice and netted passback depending on marketplace rules. For Azure private offers the simplest is an explicit reseller uplift line that Cloudwise invoices separately; alternatively we can issue a gross invoice to Helix and send a documented reseller credit.

I'll loop in our Marketplace ops (Irene) to confirm invoice flow and get a recommended uplift percentage based on the commitment profile. I attached a draft pricing spreadsheet (pricing_proposal.xlsx) with a couple of options — option A: minimal anchor + 8% reseller uplift; option B: conservative anchor + 12% uplift.

Next steps: Irene, can you confirm the recommended default for Azure PO routing and whether Helix's preference (separate reseller line) would be supported without additional billing lead time?

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Attachment: pricing_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — usage flex anchor & channel uplift details

Looping Camila in — she owns channel commissioning for Azure POs.

James / Marcus —

Short version on mechanics: for Azure marketplace private offers we have two common flows:

1) Reseller-passback (recommended): Azure pays Redwood, Redwood issues a separate credit/invoice to the reseller. The reseller then invoices Helix. This is cleaner for tax/commission tracking but requires reseller onboarding in our ERP (takes ~7 business days).

2) Single-invoice with uplift line: Redwood invoices Helix for the full amount; we include a discrete "reseller uplift" line that the customer then pays to the reseller. This is faster from a provisioning standpoint but creates gross-to-net tracking in accounting.

Operational considerations:
- If Helix prefers path (1) we need the reseller's legal name, tax ID, and billing contact to add to our vendor list.
- Uplift percentage should be agreed in the SOW and mirrored in the PO metadata to avoid reconciliation drift.
- If there is a usage anchor we tag it on the PO as "node-hour minimum" with a monthly true-up process.

Recommendation: for spiky workloads go with minimal anchor (3 node-hours/day equivalent) + reseller-passback. For uplift I suggest 10% as a starting point (flex to 8%/12% depending on commitment).

Camila — can you confirm whether onboarding Cloudwise will require any additional exceptions for Azure marketplaces?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Marketplace Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — usage flex anchor & channel uplift details

Thanks — quick operational note from channel side:

- Cloudwise onboarding: we already have Cloudwise in our vendor registry but they are not yet enabled for automatic passback on Azure. Enabling passback requires: reseller vendor ID (which I have), a signed reseller agreement (I can accept a scanned PDF), and the reseller billing contact. Once we have those, passback can be enabled in 3-5 business days.

- Proposed uplift: 10% uplift on metered usage, represented as an explicit "reseller uplift" credit line on Cloudwise invoices. We'll surface the uplift line in the SOW and in our pricing_proposal.xlsx sheet 2. Reconciliation will be monthly with a one-month lag.

- Anchor proposal for Helix: 3-month ramp baseline = month 1 at 40% expected usage, month 2 at 70%, month 3 at 100% with monthly true-ups. This avoids overcommitting while giving Cloudwise visibility for capacity planning.

If Helix agrees to the reseller-passback flow, I'll prepare the onboarding checklist and the minimal addendum to the SOW. Marcus — can you confirm whether Helix is OK with a 10% uplift and provide reseller billing contact?

Camila Reyes
Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Marcus / Camila —

Thanks for the clear options. Helix is comfortable with the reseller-passback flow (path 1) and the 10% uplift, provided the uplift is shown as a discrete line in monthly reconciliation and not hidden as a net adjustment.

Reseller billing contact: Cloudwise Inc. — accounts@cloudwise.io, Tax ID: 98-7654321.

On the anchor: we'd prefer the 3-month ramp but ask that month 1 start at 50% expected usage instead of 40% to account for an early pilot. Can you update the SOW and pricing sheet and send a DocuSign link for signature?

If we get the updated SOW today we can route to legal and procurement for signature tomorrow.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

James
